title: kubectl cluster access
whyItMatters: The kube folder holds cluster addresses and embedded client certificates or tokens. With it a stranger can talk to the clusters the person administered, and the names show which company systems they touched.
source: Kubernetes docs, organizing cluster access: kubeconfig defaults to $HOME/.kube/config: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/organize-cluster-access-kubeconfig/
notes: config is the default kubeconfig; cache holds discovery and http caches. KUBECONFIG can point somewhere else and some tools write several files into this folder.

cleanup.exportFirst: Copy any cluster configuration you still need to a secure place before removal; the copy still grants cluster access, so keep it on an encrypted drive.
cleanup.signOut: Have the cluster administrator revoke the client certificates or tokens used from this machine.
steps: Delete the folder named in the plan using your file manager.
cleanup.risk: Removes access credentials, cluster endpoints, and client certificates for all configured Kubernetes clusters.
cleanup.source: Kubernetes Documentation, Organizing Cluster Access Using kubeconfig Files: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/organize-cluster-access-kubeconfig/
